open_questions: Odd-even difference diff_sigma 3.431 depth_odd 5852 ppm vs depth_even 3792 ppm (ratio 1.5) and secondary snr 4.112 depth 549.7 ppm are below the 5-sigma threshold but non-zero; SPOC vs QLP dominates odd/even sectors, higher-precision follow-up photometry would test for true depth asymmetry.

Gaia RUWE 1.015 and non_single_star 0 plus rv_log_p -0.01129 give no binary sign, but star_density_penalty 80.71 indicates period/density mismatch, likely from spot evolution on this VARIABLE Teff 3772 K M dwarf.
dossier.public_summary: TESS shows a 4.9 Rearth flat-bottomed 4-hour dip every 13.2 days on a nearby M dwarf. Depth changes between sectors are a pipeline calibration difference, not a real change, and no neighbour bright enough to cause the dip exists. The combined size and shape, on-target light, and binarity checks make a planet the best explanation, with residual odd-even and secondary hints likely from measurement systematics that higher-resolution follow-up can test.

reasons.why: No star within one TESS pixel can cause the 4971 ppm dip even with a deep eclipse; off-target blend ruled out by distance and contratio 0.1717.
Significantly flat-bottomed (negative v_sigma) favours planet over grazing/V and duration 1.323 fits a central transit of the 0.587 R_sun M dwarf.
Planet-sized radius well below stellar regime and duration ratio matches stellar density, no stellar-eclipse warning.
p_constant 0.0008274 is a calibration offset between QLP and SPOC, not true astrophysical change (SPOC alone p_constant 0.0389), so depth change does not indicate a binary.
